articles.headline: Philadelphia Annual Conference (editorial note)
articles.summary: We hope all the brethren belonging to the Philadelphia Annual Conference will carefully observe the notice of Bishop Wayman, which appears in this week's paper. The Conference is announced to convene on the 13th of May.

articles.headline: Notice: Philadelphia Annual Conference to meet in Union Church, Coates street
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church will meet in the Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, on Saturday, May 13th, 1865. Candidates for admission and orders will do well to meet the Committee for Examination the day before the Conference convenes. A. W. Wayman. Baltimore, April 19, 1865.

articles.headline: Germantown Circuit
articles.author: Peter Gardiner
articles.summary: Brother Editor: I desire to let you know, that during the present Conference year, at each appointment, the Lord has been very propitious. At a meeting lately held in the Germantown church, eighteen professed to have found the pearl of great price, and twenty-three joined on probation. In the four appointments altogether, seventy-six have professed, and sixty-four have joined the circuit. April 19, 1865.

articles.headline: Notice: Literary Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference
articles.author: Peter Gardiner
articles.summary: The Literary Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church are requested to meet in the basement [VERIFY] of Bethel Church on Wednesday morning, May 10th, at 9 o'clock. By order of the President, Peter Gardiner. Rev. H. W. Winder [VERIFY], Sec'y.

articles.headline: Notice: "We mourn, our Chief has fallen" (Fair of the Ladies' Union Association postponed)
articles.summary: On account of our great national calamity the Fair of the Ladies' Union Association will be postponed until the 1[?]th of May [VERIFY]. The tickets already issued will be good for that time. The Fair will continue two weeks. By order of the President. S. Lizzie Brown, Sec'y. P.S. The Association returns thanks to the Ladies' Union Association of Harrisburg for a donation, and to Miss Amelia Williams [VERIFY] for money collected in Harrisburg.
people: secretary, Ladies' Union Association (also printed S. L. Brown)

articles.headline: Meeting in Frankford
articles.summary: Frankford, April 1[9], 1865 [VERIFY day]. Dear Recorder: In compliance with the order issued by the Secretary of State, our church was open for the sympathizing friends of the late Abraham Lincoln, President of the United States. The United Daughters of America, No. 2, the United Benevolent Daughters of Davis [VERIFY], and the Equal Rights League of the first district of Philadelphia formed in procession, and proceeded to the church, where they were addressed by several gentlemen. Signed by a committee of four.
people: pastor (Rev.); opened the exercises, spoke, pronounced the benediction
speaker; signs as H. Davis, Jr., committee

articles.headline: Camp William Penn
articles.author: A. B.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Since my first communication appeared in the Recorder, I have been solicited by numerous friends, in and about the camp, and by letters from the army of the Potomac, to continue my notes about Camp Penn. Sunday, April 9th, was quite an interesting day, being the day of Thanksgiving for our recent victories. Signed A. B., Chelton Hill, Pa., April 21st, 1865.

articles.headline: Florida Correspondence (3d U. S. Colored Troops)
articles.author: William B. D. Johnson
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Having a few leisure moments, I will employ them in writing a few lines to your most valuable paper. I have no doubt but some of our friends home would like to hear from the 3d regiment of U. S. Colored troops. A detachment of fifteen men made a very successful raid into the interior of the State on the 20th of March last. April 7th, 1865.
people: guide, 3d U.S.C.T.; son of Rev. John M. Brown of West Chester, Pennsylvania; wounded in the hand

articles.headline: Obituary: B. F. Brown, superintendent of Macedonia Sabbath School, Camden
articles.author: Parnell
articles.summary: Dear Recorder: I am about to inform your many readers of the very sad loss of our beloved and faithful friend and superintendent, B. F. Brown. A great man has fallen, and in the Macedonia Sabbath School a link of chain has been broken; the Sabbath School army has lost its general who, for the last six years, had so faithfully led it. Brother Brown leaves a dear wife and a number of relatives. Signed Parnell, Camden, N. J., April 1[9]th, 1865.
people: deceased; superintendent of Macedonia Sabbath School, Camden, N. J., for six years

articles.headline: Died (Frankford; Fair Haven, N. J.)
articles.summary: Died, at Frankford, on Saturday, April 1st, 1865, Mr. Henry Jeffers [VERIFY], in the 7[?]th year of his age. His funeral sermon will be preached on Sunday, May 7th, at the A. M. E. Bethel Church, Frankford. Also: died at Fair Haven, N. J., Emeline Jamison [VERIFY], a member of A. M. E. Bethel Church.

articles.headline: Letter from Rev. J. C. Gibbs
articles.author: J. C. Gibbs
articles.summary: Wilmington, N. C., April 15, 1865 [VERIFY day]. Mr. Editor: I arrived safely in Newbern on the eighth day after my departure from Philadelphia, being detained in New York four days waiting for a steamer. Sections follow on the refugees and their condition, the schools, the churches and the Presbyterian church; he has charge of the Second Presbyterian Church of Wilmington and has gathered a congregation of three or four hundred persons, both black and white.

articles.headline: Great Exhibition of the A. M. E. Zion Mission Sabbath School
articles.summary: To be given on next Wednesday Evening, the 10th instant, at the Zion Church, in Seventh street below Dickerson. We hope that our citizens will encourage and sustain Rev. Brother Winder, the pastor over the school, in his praiseworthy efforts. Let the house be filled on the evening in question.

articles.headline: Last Quarterly Meeting in Bethel Church
articles.summary: Last Sabbath was the occasion for the last Quarterly Meeting for Bethel church, (for this year,) of which Rev. William Moore is now the pastor. Brother Moore has had quite a revival during the last month or so, in his church, and a good number have professed a hope in Christ Jesus the Lord. On last Friday night the General Class met, and on Monday night the sacred ordinance of Love Feast was observed.

articles.headline: Our Correspondence somewhat interesting (Rev. J. C. Gibbs of the Seventh street Presbyterian church)
articles.summary: We refer our readers to Rev. H. M. Turner's letter, chaplain in the U. S. Army, from our old home, or near it, Raleigh, N. C. We have also received a very interesting letter from Rev. J. C. Gibbs, of the Seventh street Presbyterian church, (colored,) of this city. We refer our readers to his letter on the first page of our paper.
people: of the Seventh street Presbyterian church (colored), Philadelphia (Rev.); now in Wilmington, N. C.

articles.headline: Conferences
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church will meet in this city on the 13th of this month. Charleston, S. C.: this Conference will be re-organized by Bishop Payne, assisted by other ministers of the A. M. E. Church, as soon as practicable. The New York Conference will meet on the 10th of June [VERIFY day]; the New England Conference will also meet on the same day.

articles.headline: Institute for Colored Youth
articles.summary: The thirteenth Annual Commencement of the above named Institute took place on last Thursday, and continued till Friday night. This is one of the best schools in the city, and Professor Bassett and his corps of teachers deserve great credit for the proficiency to which they have, through great exertion, brought it.

articles.headline: Notice: Philadelphia Annual Conference; annual and missionary sermons at Bethel
articles.author: A. W. Wayman
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church will meet in the Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia, Penna., on Saturday, May 13th, 1865. The annual sermon to the Conference will be preached on Monday afternoon, May 15th, at 4 o'clock, by Rev. Henry Davis. The Missionary sermon on Thursday afternoon, May 18th, at 4 o'clock, by Rev. Joshua A. Woodlyn. These services will take place in Bethel Church on Sixth street. May 1st, 1865.
people: to preach the Missionary sermon (Rev.; printed Woodlyn)

articles.headline: Notice: James H. Teagle's first Grand Concert
articles.summary: James H. Teagle's first Grand Concert will take place on Monday evening, May 8th, at Concert Hall. The two grand pianos used upon this occasion will be procured from Chickering & Sons. The following named artists will participate in the entertainment: Madam Brown, A. S. Purnell [VERIFY middle initial], W. F. Sturgis, New York; J. D. Cliff, and J. H. Teagle.
people: gives the concert; also printed J. H. Teagle

articles.headline: Notice: "We mourn, our Chief has fallen" (Fair of the Ladies' Union Association postponed until the 15th of May)
articles.summary: On account of our great national calamity the Fair of the Ladies' Union Association will be postponed until the 15th of May. The tickets already issued will be good for that time. The Fair will continue two weeks. By order of the President. S. Lizzie Brown, Sec'y. P. S. The above named Association return their thanks to the Ladies' Union Association of Harrisburg, for their donation of $40; also, to Miss Amelia Williams, for $60, collected in Harrisburg. Miss E. Mills, President. S. L. Brown, Secretary.
people: secretary, Ladies' Union Association (also printed S. L. Brown)
president, Ladies' Union Association (printed Miss E. Mills)

articles.headline: Notice: corner stone of the new A. M. E. Church at Eversham, New Jersey
articles.author: T. Gould
articles.summary: The Lord willing, the corner stone of the new A. M. E. Church, at Eversham, New Jersey, will be laid on Thursday, the 18th day of May, 1865, exercises to commence at 2 o'clock, P. M. Bishop Wayman and other prominent ministers of the gospel are expected to be present on the occasion. We would like to raise $100 on the occasion. T. Gould, Minister in charge.

articles.headline: A Card: Mrs. Rebecca O'Donnell, boarding house, Lombard Street
articles.summary: A Card. Mrs. Rebecca O'Donnell, formerly of No. 740 South Sixth St., Philada., has removed to No. 913 [VERIFY number] Lombard Street, and has opened a Boarding House for the accommodation of Ladies and Gentlemen who may pass through Philadelphia, and also those who may wish to spend some time in our city. Give her a call.
people: proprietor of a boarding house, Lombard Street; formerly of No. 740 South Sixth St. (Mrs.)

articles.headline: Private Boarding at 633 Pine Street
articles.summary: Private Boarding at 633 Pine Street, Philadelphia. The Subscriber, having fitted up his house, takes pleasure in announcing to his friends and acquaintances travelling, that he is prepared to accommodate them when visiting the city. Warm and Cold Baths. R. H. Gleaves, Proprietor. The card is dated April 22.
people: proprietor, private boarding house, 633 Pine Street

articles.headline: The Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church
articles.summary: The Forty-ninth Session of the Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church, assembled in the A. M. E. Union Church, at 9 o'clock, A. M., Bishop Wayman presiding, assisted by Rev. Wm. P. Quinn, senior Bishop. Bishop Wayman opened the Conference by reading the fourth chapter of Second Corinthians. On motion, Rev. J. Woodlyn was appointed Secretary of the Conference, and Brother W. W. Winder assistant Secretary.
people: Secretary of the Conference (Rev.; also printed Joshua Woodlyn)
assistant Secretary; elected to Elders' orders
received from the Baltimore Annual Conference (Rev.)
received from the Baltimore Annual Conference (Rev.)
received from the Baltimore Annual Conference (Rev.)
received from the Baltimore Annual Conference (Rev.)
editor of the Christian Recorder; appointed reporter for the daily newspapers (Rev.)
conducted religious services, second day (as printed)

articles.headline: Monument to President Lincoln
articles.summary: We copy the following from the Anglo-African, and heartily approve of the proposition. It is but just to the memory of the martyred hero that the colored Americans should do something to perpetuate the name of one who sacrificed every thing, even life itself, in defending the rights of down-trodden humanity. The letter of M. R. Delany, Major 104th Regt. U. S. C. T. (Charleston, S. C., April 20th, '65), proposes a one cent contribution from every individual of the race and names as common Treasurer Rev. Stephen Smith, Philadelphia.
people: of Philadelphia (Rev.); proposed by M. R. Delany as common Treasurer of the Lincoln monument fund

articles.headline: Bishop Campbell's Arrival
articles.summary: Bishop Campbell arrived here from California, on last Monday evening, the 15th inst. The Bishop made his appearance in the Conference room, on Tuesday morning, quite unexpectedly. He is looking remarkably well, indeed.

articles.headline: Boarding and Lodging (Mrs. M. Stroder, 1132 Lombard street)
articles.summary: Mrs. M. Stroder [VERIFY surname: Stroder or Strader], of 1132 Lombard street, gives notice in another column, that she can accommodate boarders and lodgers. We have no doubt but that she can make our friends first rate arrangements [the last two lines are too faint to read].

articles.headline: Notice: First class accommodations for boarders and lodgers, Mrs. Mary Stroder
articles.summary: First class accommodations for boarders and lodgers, by Mrs. Mary Stroder [VERIFY surname: Stroder or Strader], 1132 Lombard St., Philadelphia. May 20, 3t.

articles.headline: Proceedings of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights Convention
articles.summary: We have received a copy of the proceedings of the above-named convention; also, a pamphlet form of the Preamble and Constitution of the P. S. E. R. League. The first gives an accurate and minute account of the deliberations of the Convention held at Harrisburgh on Feb. 8th, 9th, and 10th. All orders should be sent to J. C. White, Jr., 717 Lombard St., Philadelphia, Pa.
people: receives orders for the Proceedings and the Constitution of the Pennsylvania State Equal Rights League, 717 Lombard St. (printed J. C. White, Jr.)

articles.headline: Married (Philadelphia; Frankford)
articles.summary: On Thursday, the 11th inst., by Rev. Elisha Weaver, in this city, Mr. Wilkerson Boardley [VERIFY], of Chester county, Penna., to Miss Mary W. [surname illegible], of York county [VERIFY], Penna. On Friday, April 28th, 1865, at the house of the officiating clergyman, by Rev. Mr. Allen, Mr. Jas. Butter [VERIFY] to Miss Violena C. Hutchinson [VERIFY], both of Frankford, Penna.

articles.headline: Obituary: Rev. Frederick T. Hall, of Union A. M. E. Church
articles.author: J. W. Randolph
articles.summary: Died, at his late residence, 1318 Callowhill street, April 9th, 1865, Rev. Frederick T. Hall, in the triumphant hope of a blessed immortality. The deceased was for many years a member of the A. M. E. Church, Union. He seemed willing to devote his time and talent in obedience to his holy vocation. He died of cancer of the face, in the 71st year of his age.
people: deceased (Rev.); of 1318 Callowhill street; member and preacher of Union A. M. E. Church; died April 9, 1865, in his 71st year

articles.headline: Obituary: Benjamin F. Brown, of Camden
articles.author: C. E. P.
articles.summary: Camden, May 1st, 1865. Died, March 29th, 1865, Mr. Benjamin F. Brown, the teacher of the Public school, and Superintendent of the Sabbath school of the Macedonia Church, to which he belonged. A great and good man has fallen. An immense concourse of people attended the funeral; the entire public seemed to share the grief of the widow.
people: deceased; teacher of the Public school and Superintendent of the Sabbath school of Macedonia Church, Camden; died March 29, 1865

articles.headline: Obituary: Junius H. Purnell (resolutions of the Dumas Dramatic Association)
articles.summary: Philadelphia, May 12th, 1865. At a meeting of the Dumas Dramatic Association, held at their room, on Thursday evening, May 11th, the following preamble and resolutions were adopted: Whereas, It has pleased an all wise Providence to remove from our midst our beloved President and companion, Junius H. Purnell [VERIFY given name]. Signed Joseph C. Davis, Vice Pres.; Robert J. H. Johnson, Treas.; James E. Harris, Secretary.

articles.headline: Ice Cream Saloon: J. J. Lyons, No. 1023 Lombard Street
articles.summary: Ice Cream Saloon. J. J. Lyons, No. 1023 Lombard Street, Philada., invites all lovers of Ice-Cream and other delicacies to give him a call.
people: proprietor, Ice Cream Saloon, No. 1023 Lombard Street

articles.headline: The Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church (concluded; with the appointments)
articles.summary: Wednesday morning, May 17. Conference met pursuant to adjournment, Bishop Wayman in the chair. Religious services were conducted by the Rev. Wm. W. Grimes, of the New England Conference. Revs. James Hamilton, of the New York Conference, and W. W. Grimes and J. Mitchell, of the New England Conference, were introduced to the Conference. The report runs to Tuesday, May 23, and ends with the appointments. APPOINTMENTS AS PRINTED: Philadelphia, Pa.: A. M. E. Union Church, to be supplied; Bethel Church, W. Moore; Wesley Church, to be supplied; Zion Mission, H. J. Rhodes; West Philadelphia, to be supplied; West Chester circuit, James V. Pierce; Reading circuit, T. A. Cuff; Downingtown circuit, E. Laws [VERIFY initial]; Danville circuit, to be supplied; Lancaster circuit, J. Young; Chester and Horntown, P. Gardner; Oxford circuit, J. W. Stevenson; Attleborough circuit, Jacob Jay; Frankford circuit, Joseph H. Smith. New Jersey: Camden, G. E. Boyer; Woodbury circuit, Richard Barney [VERIFY surname]; Salem station, N. H. Turpin; Bridgeton, to be supplied; Cape May circuit, John C. Cornish; Burlington circuit, T. Gould; Bordentown circuit, James Hollen; Trenton station, Thos. H. Cooper; Princeton station, to be supplied; New Brunswick, B. Lynch; Freehold circuit, A. C. Crippen. Delaware: Wilmington, to be supplied; Lewistown, John H. Henson; Frederick, W. H. Williams; Smyrna, Gilbert Waters; Camden, Harrison Lewis; Milton, Wm. H. Turner; Penningtonville, Wm. R. Norris. Transferred: Henry Davis, Joshua Woodlyn, W. W. Winder, and Wm. Rodgers, to New York Conference; A. L. Stanford and T. Steward, to South Carolina Conference; Redman Faucet, to Missouri Conference; Rev. Thomas W. Henry to Baltimore Conference.

articles.headline: Rev. J. B. Reeve
articles.summary: It gives us more than usual pleasure to say that Rev. J. B. Reeve, of our city, has the honor of being one of the first, if not the first, colored man ever elected as delegate to the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church. Mr. Reeve has, since he has been pastor of Central Presbyterian Church, greatly endeared himself to our citizens, and is considered one of the ablest divines in our midst.
people: pastor of Central Presbyterian Church (Rev.); elected alternate delegate to the New School Presbyterian General Assembly

articles.headline: A Visit to the Old Folks' Home
articles.summary: On Saturday evening last, Conference visited the Old Folks' Home, on Front street, between Spruce and Pine. This Institution, which has been established for the purpose of taking care of the aged colored people, is under the management of a white and colored Board of Directors. We were kindly received by brother Morris Hall, and the matron, who is a white woman.
people: received the Conference at the Old Folks' Home, Front street between Spruce and Pine (brother)

articles.headline: Sabbath School Anniversary
articles.summary: The anniversary of the Sabbath schools connected with the different churches in the city, which took place on Monday last, the 22d inst., in the Bethel church, was attended with great success. Addresses were made by Revs. Stephen Smith, Turpen, and Woodlyn. Dr. Armstrong also made a short speech, after which he presented a splendid silk banner to the Sabbath school class which had collected the most Missionary money; the infant class of Bethel Church, under the charge of Miss Esther Armstrong, carried off the prize.
people: in charge of the infant class of Bethel Church Sabbath school (Miss)

articles.headline: Notice: whereabouts of William Johnson, Christopher Carter and Elias Harris
articles.author: Annie Jackson
articles.summary: Can any one inform me of the whereabouts of Mr. William Johnson, Christopher Carter, or Elias Harris, from Washington, D. C., who left there, on Saturday, the 13th inst., for Philadelphia, and were going thence to Boston, Mass. Having lost the card they left with me, I cannot tell where to find them. Any information in respect to them will be very thankfully received at No. 612 Locust street, opposite Washington Square.

articles.headline: Indiana and Missouri Conferences
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: The ministers and members of the Indiana Conference are hereby notified, that the Annual Conference, for this District, will be held in the city of Springfield, State of Illinois, commencing at the hour of 9 o'clock, A. M., on Saturday, August 12th, 1865. J. P. Campbell, Presiding Bishop. Philadelphia, May 24th, 1865. A second notice calls the Missouri Conference at New Orleans.

articles.headline: Died: Anna M. Till, wife of Rev. Andrew Till of the Philadelphia Conference
articles.summary: Died. At Glen R[...], Penna. [VERIFY place], on May 13th, Anna M. Till, wife of Rev. Andrew Till, of the Philadelphia Conference, in the sixty fifth year of her age.
people: deceased, May 13, 1865, in her sixty fifth year; wife of Rev. Andrew Till
of the Philadelphia Conference (Rev.); husband of the deceased

articles.summary: Military Instruction given to Companies, Associations, &c. Terms Moderate. Address James J. Spelman, 1021 [VERIFY number] South Street, Philadelphia.

articles.summary: W. R. DeCordover's Periodical Depot, 419 South Seventh Street, Philada. Daily and Weekly papers always on hand. New York Ledger, Anglo-African, Harper's Weekly, &c., for sale. Also, Stationery.

articles.summary: James C. Clark, M. D. (Eclectic.) No. 618 Pine Street, Philadelphia, Pennsylv'a. Office hours: from 7 to 9 A. M., from 12 to 2 P. M., from 6 to 9 P. M. Also, particular attention directed to all classes of Ulcers, recent or chronic. Treatment and cure, without the use of Mercury or any other injurious drug, warranted. The card is dated January 7.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- session called
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman's notice, dated Baltimore, April 19, 1865: the Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church will meet in the Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia, on Saturday, May 13th, 1865. Candidates for admission and orders are to meet the Committee for Examination the day before the Conference convenes. An editorial note on page 2 asks all the brethren to observe the notice.

events.name: Literary Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- meeting called
events.location: Bethel Church, Philadelphia (the notice appears to read 'in the basement of Bethel Church' [VERIFY])
events.description: The Literary Association of the Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church is requested to meet at Bethel Church on Wednesday morning, May 10th, at 9 o'clock. By order of the President, Peter Gardiner. The secretary's name is printed faintly: Rev. H. W. Winder [VERIFY]. The notice is marked to run twice.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association -- Fair postponed on account of the death of President Lincoln
events.location: Philadelphia (place of the Fair not stated in the notice)
events.description: Notice headed 'We mourn, our Chief has fallen.' On account of the national calamity the Fair of the Ladies' Union Association is postponed until the 1[?]th of May [VERIFY: the day is not legible]; tickets already issued will be good for that time; the Fair will continue two weeks. By order of the President; S. Lizzie Brown, Sec'y. A postscript returns the thanks of the Association to the Ladies' Union Association of Harrisburg for a donation and to Miss Amelia Williams [VERIFY] for money collected in Harrisburg, signed by the President, Miss E. M[...] [VERIFY: surname not legible] and S. L. Brown, Secretary.

events.name: Frankford -- memorial meeting for President Lincoln at the A. M. E. church
events.description: Letter dated Frankford, April 1[9], 1865 (the printed day is unclear; April 19 was the day of the national obsequies ordered by the Secretary of State). The church was opened for the sympathizing friends of the late Abraham Lincoln. The United Daughters of America, No. 2, the United Benevolent Daughters of Davis [VERIFY name], and the Equal Rights League of the first district of Philadelphia formed in procession and proceeded to the church. Rev. Henderson Davis opened with singing and prayer and spoke; Mr. Henderson Davis, Jr. spoke next; Mr. Jo[...] Trusty, Esq. [VERIFY given name] was the third speaker; Rev. Samuel Murray closed, saying that as God placed Joshua in Moses' stead so He would place Andrew Johnson in Abraham Lincoln's stead, and gave out a hymn. Benediction by Rev. Henderson Davis. Signed by a committee: Lewis N. B[...] [VERIFY surname], H. Davis, Jr., J. G. Lee [VERIFY], Wm. S. Walker.

events.name: Camp William Penn -- Thanksgiving, Easter and Lincoln memorial services (24th U.S.C.T.)
events.location: Camp William Penn, Chelton Hill, Pa.
events.description: Letter signed A. B., Chelton Hill, April 21st, 1865. Sunday, April 9th, the day of Thanksgiving: the chaplain, Rev. Henry Austier [VERIFY spelling], read Governor Curtin's Proclamation; in the evening Rev. B. Faucett [VERIFY] preached from Hebrews 12: 1, 2; about midnight the cry was heard in camp that Lee and his whole army had surrendered. Easter Sunday, April 16th: Rev. Dr. Parvin preached on the Resurrection and compared the death of the Saviour to the martyrdom of the President. Wednesday morning, April 19th: Col. Wagner had the War Department orders on the obsequies read to the 24th regiment U. S. colored troops by Adjutant Milliken [VERIFY], and Dr. Parvin preached on the life and death of Abraham Lincoln, saying the time had come when soldiers, white and black, were known only as soldiers.

events.name: A. M. E. Zion Mission Sabbath School -- Great Exhibition
events.location: Zion Church, Seventh street below Dickerson, Philadelphia
events.description: Editorial notice: a Great Exhibition of the A. M. E. Zion Mission Sabbath School is to be given on Wednesday evening, the 10th instant, at the Zion Church in Seventh street below Dickerson. The paper asks the citizens to encourage and sustain 'Rev. Brother Winder, the pastor over the school' (surname only as printed).

events.name: Bethel Church -- last Quarterly Meeting of the Conference year
events.description: The last Quarterly Meeting for Bethel church for the Conference year was held 'last Sabbath' (April 30, 1865). Rev. William Moore is now the pastor and has had a revival during the last month. The General Class met on Friday night and the Love Feast was observed on Monday night. A number of white friends of different denominations (Methodists, Presbyterians and Baptists) were present.

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth -- thirteenth Annual Commencement
events.description: The thirteenth Annual Commencement of the Institute took place 'on last Thursday, and continued till Friday night' (May 4 and 5, 1865). The editor credits Professor Bassett and his corps of teachers. No class list is printed in this issue.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- annual and missionary sermons announced
events.location: Conference at Union Church, Coates street; the sermons at Bethel Church on Sixth street, Philadelphia
events.description: Bishop A. W. Wayman's second notice, dated May 1st, 1865: the Conference meets in the Union Church, Coates street, on Saturday, May 13th, 1865. The annual sermon to the Conference will be preached on Monday afternoon, May 15th, at 4 o'clock, by Rev. Henry Davis; the Missionary sermon on Thursday afternoon, May 18th, at 4 o'clock, by Rev. Joshua A. Woodlyn (as printed). Both services in Bethel Church on Sixth street. The examining committees are to meet the candidates the day before the Conference convenes.

events.description: Notice headed 'We mourn, our Chief has fallen' (first printed April 29; this is the clearer impression). The Fair of the Ladies' Union Association is postponed until the 15th of May; tickets already issued will be good; the Fair will continue two weeks. By order of the President; S. Lizzie Brown, Sec'y. Postscript: the Association thanks the Ladies' Union Association of Harrisburg for their donation of $40, and Miss Amelia Williams for $60 collected in Harrisburg. Miss E. Mills, President; S. L. Brown, Secretary.

events.name: A. M. E. Church at Eversham, New Jersey -- laying of the corner stone
events.description: The corner stone of the new A. M. E. Church at Eversham, New Jersey, is to be laid on Thursday, May 18th, 1865, exercises to commence at 2 o'clock P. M. Bishop Wayman and other ministers are expected. The church hopes to raise $100 on the occasion. Signed T. Gould, Minister in charge.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- forty-ninth session, first three days
events.location: A. M. E. Union Church, Coates street, near Fifth, Philadelphia
events.description: First day (Saturday, May 13, 1865, 9 A.M.): Bishop Wayman presiding, assisted by Rev. Wm. P. Quinn, senior Bishop. Elder Moore led in prayer. Rev. J. Woodlyn appointed Secretary and Brother W. W. Winder assistant Secretary. Rev. Benjamin Lynch, transferred from the Ohio Conference, and Revs. N. A. Turpen, Geo. E. Boyer, W. H. Williams and H. J. Rhodes, from the Baltimore Annual Conference, were confirmed as members. Standing committees appointed; examination of characters until one o'clock. Rev. E. Weaver, editor of the Christian Recorder, appointed reporter for the daily newspapers. Second day (Monday, May 15): Bishop Quinn in the chair; religious services by Rev. John H. Henson and A. C. Cuppen (as printed); committee reports; brethren offered for membership referred to the Committee on Membership; financial reports; at 4 P.M. adjourned to hear the annual sermon by Rev. Henry Davis; the Missionary sermon announced for Bethel Church on Thursday the 18th by Rev. Joshua Woodlyn. Third day (Tuesday, May 16): Bishop Wayman presiding, assisted by Bishop Quinn; the complaint against Rev. Brother Jay withdrawn; the application of Rev. Brother J. H. Smith for confirmation to membership withdrawn; Isaiah Broaden, admitted last year, dropped from the roll for leaving his circuit without notifying the Bishop; Brothers Thos. H. Cooper, John C. Cornish and W. W. Winder elected to Elders' orders; Revs. J. G. Beulah and Sheppard Holcomb continued on the superannuated list. Bishop Campbell, just back from California (he arrived Monday evening the 15th), walked up the aisle and took his seat on the platform. Adjourned to Wednesday at 9 o'clock. The appointments are not printed in this issue.
attendees: senior Bishop; assisted, and presided on the second day
Secretary (Rev.; also printed Joshua Woodlyn); Missionary sermon
assistant Secretary; elected to Elders' orders
received by transfer from the Ohio Conference (Rev.)

events.name: Dumas Dramatic Association -- meeting on the death of its President, Junius H. Purnell
events.location: the Association's room, Philadelphia (address not given)
events.description: At a meeting of the Dumas Dramatic Association held at their room on Thursday evening, May 11th, 1865, a preamble and resolutions were adopted on the death of 'our beloved President and companion, Junius H. Purnell' [VERIFY given name: the small capitals are blurred]: sympathy with the bereaved parents of the deceased; the members to wear a badge of mourning for thirty days; the proceedings to be sent to the parents and published in the Sunday Despatch and Christian Recorder; the Association to attend the funeral in a body. Signed Joseph C. Davis, Vice Pres.; Robert J. H. Johnson, Treas.; James E. Harris, Secretary. Dated Philadelphia, May 12th, 1865.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- forty-ninth session, May 17 to 23, and the appointments for 1865-66
events.location: A. M. E. Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia
events.description: Wednesday May 17: Bishop Wayman in the chair; services by Rev. Wm. W. Grimes of the New England Conference; Revs. James Hamilton (New York Conference), W. W. Grimes and J. Mitchell (New England Conference) introduced; two local preachers of the Zion Mission church elected to Deacon's orders if they stand examination; the death of Rev. F. T. Hall, local preacher of the A. M. E. Union Church, laid before Conference. Thursday May 18: services by Rev. Joseph H. Smith; the Editor and General Book Steward made his annual report; Bishop Wayman, called away to lay the corner stone of a new church in the Burlington Circuit, placed Rev. Thomas Henry in the chair; the Committee on Ordination reported in favor of ordaining four deacons. Friday May 19: Bishops Wayman, Quinn and Campbell; services by Rev. Wm. H. Chase of the New England District; Bishop Campbell asked Conference for a man for California. Saturday May 20: services by Rev. Theodore Gould; report on the Book Concern adopted; on the report of the Committee on the State of the Country the speakers were Rev. Mr. Flannery, agent of the Methodist Tract Society of Philadelphia, Rev. J. Mitchell, Rev. Wm. H. Jones of Canada and Rev. Stephen Smith; laid over on motion of Elisha Weaver. Monday May 22: services by Rev. N. H. Turpin; a resolution of condolence 'with the widow of the late Andrew Till' offered by E. Weaver (see the death notice on page 3, which names the wife as the deceased); on the State of the Country Elisha Weaver, Mr. Isaiah Weare, Friend Hood [VERIFY], Rev. Mr. Patterson of the M. E. Church, Rev. Mr. Cookman, pastor of the M. E. Church on Fourth street between Market and Arch, Brother Mitchell and Bishop Campbell spoke, and the report was adopted unanimously. The Conference then sat as a Missionary Society and elected: President, Rev. Stephen Smith; Vice President, Rev. Wm. Moore; Secretary, Elisha Weaver; Treasurer, Rev. J. P. B. Eddy; Executive Committee, Revs. Joseph Eddy, Nelson A. Turpen, James Hollin, James Frisby, Benj. Lynch, R. P. Gibbs, Joseph H. Smith and Wm. Williams; dues paid in, $27. Tuesday May 23: thanks to The Press for publishing the daily proceedings; total Missionary money collected $940.97 [VERIFY first digit]; $250 to be sent to Bro. Davis at Baltimore. THE APPOINTMENTS AS PRINTED: Philadelphia, Pa.: A. M. E. Union Church, to be supplied; Bethel Church, W. Moore; Wesley Church, to be supplied; Zion Mission, H. J. Rhodes; West Philadelphia, to be supplied; West Chester circuit, James V. Pierce; Reading circuit, T. A. Cuff; Downingtown circuit, E. Laws [VERIFY initial]; Danville circuit, to be supplied; Lancaster circuit, J. Young; Chester and Horntown, P. Gardner; Oxford circuit, J. W. Stevenson; Attleborough circuit, Jacob Jay; Frankford circuit, Joseph H. Smith. New Jersey: Camden, G. E. Boyer; Woodbury circuit, Richard Barney [VERIFY surname]; Salem station, N. H. Turpin; Bridgeton, to be supplied; Cape May circuit, John C. Cornish; Burlington circuit, T. Gould; Bordentown circuit, James Hollen; Trenton station, Thos. H. Cooper; Princeton station, to be supplied; New Brunswick, B. Lynch; Freehold circuit, A. C. Crippen. Delaware: Wilmington, to be supplied; Lewistown, John H. Henson; Frederick, W. H. Williams; Smyrna, Gilbert Waters; Camden, Harrison Lewis; Milton, Wm. H. Turner; Penningtonville, Wm. R. Norris. Transferred: Henry Davis, Joshua Woodlyn, W. W. Winder, and Wm. Rodgers, to New York Conference; A. L. Stanford and T. Steward, to South Carolina Conference; Redman Faucet, to Missouri Conference; Rev. Thomas W. Henry to Baltimore Conference. E. Weaver was elected District Book Steward. The next session is to meet at Princeton, New Jersey, on the second Saturday in May, 1866.

events.name: Missionary Society of the Philadelphia Annual Conference -- election of officers
events.location: A. M. E. Union Church, Coates street, Philadelphia
events.description: On Monday, May 22, 1865, the Conference resolved itself into a Missionary Society, altered its constitution to harmonize with that of the Parent Missionary Society, and elected officers for the ensuing year: President, Rev. Stephen Smith; Vice President, Rev. Wm. Moore; Secretary, Elisha Weaver; Treasurer, Rev. J. P. B. Eddy; Executive Committee, Revs. Joseph Eddy, Nelson A. Turpen, James Hollin, James Frisby, Benj. Lynch, R. P. Gibbs, Joseph H. Smith, and Wm. Williams. Bros. Stephen Smith and Moore were installed; members enrolled and paid dues to the amount of $27. The Society met again on Tuesday the 23d: cash receipts $36 [VERIFY]; total Missionary money collected $940.97 [VERIFY first digit].
attendees: President, Conference Missionary Society (Rev.); spoke on the State of the Country
Secretary, Conference Missionary Society; elected District Book Steward (also printed E. Weaver)
executive committee (Rev.; printed Hollin here, Hollen in the appointments)

events.name: Anniversary of the Sabbath schools of the city churches
events.description: The anniversary of the Sabbath schools connected with the different churches in the city took place on Monday, May 22, 1865, in the Bethel church, which was crowded. Addresses by Revs. Stephen Smith, Turpen and Woodlyn. Dr. Armstrong made a short speech and presented a silk banner to the Sabbath school class which had collected the most Missionary money: the infant class of Bethel Church, under the charge of Miss Esther Armstrong. The Doctor promised a like present next year. The Bethel Sabbath school, through its superintendent (not named), contributed $50 [VERIFY amount] to the Missionary cause.
attendees: teacher in charge of the Bethel infant class (Miss)

events.name: Visit of the Conference to the Old Folks' Home
events.location: Old Folks' Home, Front street, between Spruce and Pine, Philadelphia
events.description: On Saturday evening, May 20, 1865, the Conference visited the Old Folks' Home on Front street between Spruce and Pine, established to care for aged colored people and managed by a white and colored Board of Directors. The visitors were received by brother Morris Hall and the matron (a white woman, not named), were shown through the apartments, and had prayer with the inmates.

SECOND PASS (2026-11-14), coverage. Read from image crops, every column top to bottom: Apr 29 p1 (frame 17) cols 1-7; Apr 29 p4 (frame 20) cols 1-7; May 6 p1 (frame 21) cols 1-7; May 6 true p4 (frame 23) cols 1-7; May 6 true p3 (frame 24) cols 3-7 in full; May 20 p1 (frame 26) cols 1-7; May 20 p4 (frame 29) cols 1-7; May 27 p1 (frame 30) cols 1-7; May 27 p4 (frame 33) cols 1-7; and the advertising columns 5-7 of page 3 in every issue. SECOND PASS, what could not be read: the lowest quarter of May 27 p1 (all seven columns: ends of 'To young men', 'Our Future', 'A Spring Day up the James', the 54th Mass. letter, the serial, 'Reconstruction' and the start of 'From Boston') and the lowest fifth of May 27 p4 cols 1-4 are out of focus on the film; the lowest part of May 20 p1 cols 4 and 6 (end of the Portsmouth letter, serial) and May 20 p4 cols 1-2 feet are also blurred. SECOND PASS, result of the search. No account of Lincoln's funeral in Philadelphia (April 22-24) appears on pages 1 or 4 of any of the four issues, nor on Apr 29 pages 2 and 3 (read by column in the first pass and re-checked against the OCR for the editorial columns): the Apr 29 Lincoln matter is poetry (p1), the Frankford memorial meeting and Camp William Penn services (p2), and out-of-town resolutions from Washington and Bridgeport (p3). The only funeral-procession report is from Chicago (May 20 p1, signed Ruth): the colored citizens there turned out and were cheered, John Jones went with the remains to Springfield. The New York exclusion from the procession is noted editorially May 6 p2. The Philadelphia account was most likely in the Apr 22 issue (Reader A) or the missing May 13 number.
